- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.67) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment or price; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% after a spike.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., > 10% over 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day average) to dampen noise before forecasting.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), model tends to overcorrect; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for lag.
